title: Design the Snake Game (OOD)
prompt: Design the classic Snake game. A snake moves on a grid in a direction the player controls; it grows when it eats food and the game ends when it hits a wall or itself. Model the classes, the game loop, and — importantly — the data structures that make each move O(1) rather than scanning the whole snake. Sketch the class diagram.
blurb: Deceptively simple OOD where the data structures matter — an O(1) move using a deque plus a position set for self-collision.

rubric.label: Requirements clarification
rubric.description: Clarifies grid size, controls, wall behavior (die vs wrap), food spawning, growth rule, and win condition before designing.

rubric.label: Core entities
rubric.description: Identifies Game, Board/Grid, Snake, Food, Cell/Point, Direction, and a game-loop/engine.

rubric.label: Class design
rubric.description: Snake owns its body and movement, Board owns dimensions and food, Game orchestrates ticks; no god class with a raw 2D array holding everything.

rubric.label: Data structures
rubric.description: Deque for the snake body plus a HashSet of occupied cells so each move (head add / tail remove / self-collision check) is O(1), not O(length).

rubric.label: Game loop / movement
rubric.description: A tick model: read direction, compute new head, detect collision/food, grow or move, spawn food; deterministic and testable.

rubric.label: State machine
rubric.description: Game states (RUNNING/PAUSED/GAME_OVER/WON) and transitions; rejecting input after game over; illegal 180-degree reversal.

rubric.label: API methods
rubric.description: move(direction)/tick(), changeDirection, spawnFood, isGameOver, getScore; clean signatures.

rubric.label: Edge cases
rubric.description: Wall hit, self-collision, food on the snake, reversing into itself, board full (win), simultaneous grow-and-move at start.

rubric.label: Extensibility
rubric.description: Wrap-around walls, obstacles, multiple food types/power-ups, or multiplayer slot in without rewriting movement.

rubric.label: Communication
rubric.description: Explains the O(1) move data structures clearly and reasons about the game-loop timing/collision order.

functional_requirements: Snake moves one cell per tick in the current direction on an W x H grid
Snake grows by one when its head reaches food; new food spawns on a free cell
Game ends on collision with a wall or the snake's own body
Track score; optional win when the snake fills the board
nonfunctional_requirements: Each move is O(1): head insert, tail remove, and self-collision check
Food spawns only on unoccupied cells, efficiently
Deterministic, testable tick loop (logic decoupled from rendering)
Extensible to wrap walls, obstacles, and power-ups
clarifying_questions: Do walls kill the snake or wrap around?
How fast — fixed tick rate, or does speed increase with score?
Growth: one cell per food? Multiple food items at once?
Is there a win condition (fill the board), or endless?
Single player, or is multiplayer in scope?

core_classes.name: Game / GameEngine
core_classes.responsibility: Orchestrates the tick loop: reads input, advances the snake, resolves collisions/food, updates score and game state.

core_classes.name: Board / Grid
core_classes.responsibility: Owns dimensions and current food; validates bounds; spawns food on free cells.

core_classes.name: Snake
core_classes.responsibility: Owns the body as an ordered deque plus a set of occupied cells; moves in O(1) and detects self-collision in O(1).

core_classes.name: Point / Cell
core_classes.responsibility: Immutable (row, col) coordinate; used as map/set key.

core_classes.name: Direction (enum)
core_classes.responsibility: UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT with (dr, dc) deltas and an opposite() for the no-reversal rule.

core_classes.name: Food
core_classes.responsibility: Location and effect (normal grows by 1; power-ups could grow more or change speed).

relationships: Game composes a Board and a Snake and owns the GameState
Snake composes its body Deque and occupied Set (composition)
Board has-a current Food and optional obstacles
Point is a value object keyed in the Snake's occupied set and food placement

design_patterns.why: Cleanly stop movement/input after GAME_OVER or during PAUSED.

design_patterns.where: Wall behavior (die vs wrap) and food/power-up effects
design_patterns.why: Swap rules without editing the movement core.

design_patterns.where: Renderer/score display subscribing to game events

apis: void changeDirection(Direction d) — ignored if it's a 180 reversal
state_transitions: RUNNING --tick, no collision--> RUNNING; --eats food--> RUNNING (grow, +score, spawn food)
RUNNING --hits wall or self--> GAME_OVER (reject further input)
edge_cases: Head moves into a wall -> GAME_OVER (unless wrap mode)
Head moves into a body cell -> self-collision -> GAME_OVER
Subtlety: moving into the current tail cell is legal when NOT growing (the tail vacates that cell this tick) — order the tail-remove/head-add and set check correctly
Food spawns on a snake cell -> must pick from free cells only
180-degree reversal input -> ignore (can't reverse into own neck)
Board full -> WIN, no free cell for food
Multiple direction inputs within one tick -> apply only the last valid one
concurrency: Input arrives asynchronously while the tick loop runs: buffer the latest requested direction and apply it at the next tick (single-threaded logic thread) to avoid mid-tick mutation
Keep game logic on one thread; rendering/input on others communicate via a thread-safe queue or a volatile pendingDirection
For multiplayer, serialize each tick's move resolution so two snakes' collisions are evaluated against a consistent snapshot
extensibility: Wrap-around walls: a WallStrategy that maps out-of-bounds head coordinates back onto the grid
Obstacles: add to Board's obstacle set; collision check already consults occupied/obstacle sets
Power-ups / multiple food types: Food carries an effect (extra growth, speed, shrink)
Increasing speed: tick rate as a function of score
Multiplayer: multiple Snake instances sharing a Board with per-snake occupied sets merged for collision

deep_dives.probe: What data structure holds the snake body, and how do you make each move O(1) — head add, tail remove, and checking self-collision without scanning the whole snake?
The snake's head moves into the cell its tail currently occupies. Is that a collision? Walk me through the order of tail-remove vs collision-check so it's correct whether or not the snake is growing.
How do you spawn food on a random free cell efficiently as the snake fills the board — random-retry vs maintaining a free-cell set?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions array or scan or loop through body
followup_bank.question: Checking self-collision by scanning the body is O(length) per tick. What structure gives you O(1) collision checks plus O(1) grow/move?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions deque or queue or list for body
followup_bank.question: Good — pair the deque with what so self-collision is O(1) instead of a linear search?
How do you place food only on empty cells, and does your approach degrade when the snake nearly fills the board?
How do you prevent a 180-degree reversal, and how do you handle several direction inputs arriving within one tick?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions wall or edge or collision
followup_bank.question: Where does wall-vs-wrap behavior live so you can switch it without touching the movement code?

tradeoffs: Deque + HashSet (O(1) move, extra memory for the set) vs array/list only (simpler, O(length) collision) — the set is the key insight
Random-retry food spawn (simple, slows as board fills) vs a maintained free-cell set (O(1) spawn, more bookkeeping)
Fixed tick rate (predictable) vs speed-by-score (better gameplay, more state)
WallStrategy indirection (extensible) vs an inline wrap flag (simpler now)
reference.reference_answer: A strong answer separates Game (tick loop + state), Board (dimensions, food, obstacles), and Snake (its own body and movement), rather than stuffing a 2D array into one class. The key technical insight is the Snake's representation: an ordered Deque of body Points for O(1) head-add and tail-remove, plus a HashSet of occupied Points so self-collision is O(1) instead of scanning the body. Each tick computes the next head from a Direction enum's deltas, then resolves wall/self collision, food (grow vs move), and food re-spawn. The candidate nails the tail-chase subtlety — moving into the tail's current cell is legal when not growing, which depends on ordering tail-remove before the collision check — plus no-180-reversal, food-only-on-free-cells, and the board-full win. They buffer async input into a pendingDirection applied at tick boundaries, and show wall-vs-wrap, obstacles, and power-ups extend via strategy/effect without rewriting movement.

interviewer_notes: This looks trivial and mostly tests whether the candidate reaches for the right data structures. The single biggest signal: if they check self-collision by scanning the body (O(length)), push them to a Deque + HashSet for O(1) move and collision. The subtle correctness probe is the tail-chase case — head entering the tail's vacated cell is legal when not growing; make them get the tail-remove/collision-check ordering right, because a naive occupied-set check reports a false collision. Also probe food spawning as the board fills (random-retry degrades) and the async-input buffering into the tick boundary. Keep game logic on one thread with input buffered. Over-engineering traps: threading the game loop elaborately, building a rendering engine, or an ECS framework for a single snake. If time remains, ask for wrap-around walls or power-ups to confirm movement stays closed for modification.
